decision.summary: Tom gave one month's notice on 10 Oct for 10 Nov. Under the Renters' Rights Act two months is required, so the earliest end is 10 Dec 2026. I acknowledged this to Tom, asked Ben whether he accepts 10 Nov, and started move-out steps.

answers.question: Is the notice valid as given? What is the earliest end date?
answers.answer: No. One month is too short; tenants must give two months' written notice. Served 10 Oct 2026, so the earliest end date is 10 Dec 2026.

answers.question: What options exist to end sooner?
answers.answer: Only if the landlord (Ben Hartley) agrees in writing to an earlier date such as 10 Nov; asked him by 16 Oct. A new tenant or surrender agreement would also need landlord agreement.

answers.question: What do you reply and what do you start?
answers.answer: Replied to Tom acknowledging notice, stating 10 Dec, explaining keys return, checkout with 24h notice, and deposit return via mydeposits (within 10 days of agreement). Started: landlord question, chase follow-up 16 Oct, checkout/key-return follow-up 3 Dec.

conflicts: Tenant says one month's notice; law requires two months.
assumptions: Email counts as written notice served 10 Oct 2026.
Tenancy is assured periodic per CRM.

args.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for your email of 10 October. We've received your notice and wish you luck with the new job in Manchester.

Under the current rules a tenant needs to give two months' written notice, so one month isn't enough. Counting from today, the earliest your tenancy can end is 10 December 2026. Rent stays due until then. You asked to leave on 10 November: we've asked your landlord whether they'd agree to that in writing. Until they say yes, please plan on 10 December. We'll let you know their answer, and we'll update you by Friday 16 October at the latest.

We're starting your move-out now:
- Keys: please hand all keys back to us on or before the end date. We'll confirm the exact place and time with you.
- Checkout: we'll arrange a checkout inspection around the end date and give you at least 24 hours' written notice.
- Deposit: your £2,019 deposit is protected with mydeposits. After checkout, any deductions are agreed with you or decided by the scheme's free dispute service. It's returned within 10 days of agreement.

Please reply if you have questions.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings
